source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Fresh full twelve-file enterprise-policy patch read, including all359 lines of the new browser fixture and every changed unit/manifest/doc/metric hunk. Present policy keys request locked prefs individually: DonationEnabled maps donation_enabled, SurveyEnabled maps the existing blog_enabled type, MessageEnabled maps message_enabled, and Disabled inversely sets the global enabled pref. The filter uses the type prefix before underscore, so donation, donation_tab and donation_browser share the donation flag; security has no granular flag here but global disable rejects it. The intentional bypass-filtering branch returns before policy checks, so this is not an unconditional guarantee for direct manager/test/bypass inputs. Raw JSON notification data stays unfiltered; getNotifications computes eligible candidates and the manager receives that filtered result, reusing the existing pipeline lesson. Review explicitly rejects filtering stored state because later preference changes need the original candidates without a redownload. Lazy-property mappings use Object.entries and direct iteration; the underscore-private naming criticism is rebutted as actual mapping-key identity. Global preference discoverability/default-file additions are explicitly deferred; neither proposal changes a general naming/default rule. All75 submitted review rows and complete timeline read. The donation_tab/browser failure reports are followed by type-family code and explicit tests. Browser tests cover omitted policy, three granular flags, global disable, security, tab/browser blocking and policy-engine reset/cleanup. Historical negative side-effect cases wait one second, a bounded absence check rather than a general arbitrary-delay preference; current normal negative UI helper also waits. Tests assert prefs and visible text/actions, not every runtime reload or policy-removal state. No tests ran.
title: Notification policy controls type families at the filter boundary
